## The Great Lesbian Cure & 4chan’s /aco/ Board

The most vibrant discussion this week erupted on 4chan’s /aco/ board, where a thread titled "Lesbians being cured" has dominated the conversation. The core premise explores the sexual transition of lesbian characters—specifically Emily and Tracer from *Overwatch*—into heterosexuality through intercourse with men. The debate is nuanced, pitting those who view lesbianism as a result of sexual trauma against those who argue it’s merely a preference for male anatomy ("plastic dick").

Key entities in the thread include Critical Drinker, the *Owl House*, and even bonobos, as users debate whether high-libido lesbians are essentially bisexual or exist to facilitate fantasy for straight men. The discourse draws sharp lines between "normal" lesbians and "degenerate Activists" (or "yurifags"), with opinions ranging from the phenomenon being "God intended" to criticisms of the community’s tolerance of "futa" content. Defenders of the community cite biological tests and animal behavior to argue that lesbianism is a natural, valid state.

## Geopolitics and Photography: Japan’s Neutral Stand and M4/3 Wars

On /pol/, an NHK report on a pro-Israel protest in Tokyo’s Shibuya district sparked a broader geopolitical analysis. While some users mocked the event as an American colonial display, a significant portion advocated for Japanese neutrality. Commenters argued that Japan’s strong ties with Arab countries and lack of involvement in Western history shield it from the lobbying-driven consequences seen in the U.S. The thread referenced diplomatic anecdotes, such as Benjamin Netanyahu serving Shinzo Abe dessert in a shoe, to highlight perceived slights. Ultimately, the consensus was that Japan’s distinct geopolitical position protects its citizens from global polarization.

Simultaneously, the photography community on 4chan engaged in aggressive gear-head banter regarding Micro Four Thirds (M4/3) cameras. Users argued that GoPro is the only brand effectively leveraging the sensor’s small size, while Olympus and Panasonic lag behind. Technical debates focused on the M4/3 mount’s telecentric design versus Sony’s E-mount, citing vignetting and light incidence angles. Sony was criticized for historical hardware issues, while Fujifilm was mocked for waxy skin tones. Despite the attacks, M4/3 proponents defended the platform’s reliability, dismissing claims that the system is obsolete.

## Touhou’s Whimsy and the Z5IIC Rumors

The *Touhou Project* community remains active with diverse content. Newsblur aggregates shared fan art ranging from Sanae Kochiya in the "Sacrifice" level to anthropomorphic Reimu Hakurei overlaid on tabby cats. Meanwhile, user @Dayyaful sparked discussion by creating a *sukusuku* (paper model) of Tokiko, an unnamed community-designated character. The post highlighted the effort of "revealing" obscure characters to the broader fanbase. Additionally, fans are analyzing key visuals for upcoming anime like *Denki Daisy* (2027) and *Magical★Explorers*.

In camera news, rumors suggest Nikon will announce the Z5IIC, a compact full-frame mirrorless camera positioned as a rangefinder-style competitor to the Sony a7c. Attributed features include a 24 MP sensor and IBIS in a viewfinder-less design. While some users celebrated a non-Sony option, others speculated it might be a "parts bin" update using older processors.

## Quick Hits

*   **Vintage Computing:** Collectors are sharing artifacts from the late 70s and early 80s, including Sperry software, National Checking Company data cards from 1983, and an Altair Ext Basic microcassette.
*   **Ladies and Gentlemen, We Got Em:** 4chan’s /v/ board celebrated the acquisition of a property previously owned by a "Rabbi," sparking etymological pedantry about Jewish identity and anti-Semitism. The video game of the same name also sparked excitement, with users debating if the protagonist resembles an Infowars personality.
*   **Play WEGs:** Users on /v/ curated recommendations for Western and French erotic games and films, highlighting cross-medium interest in regional adult genres.
*   **Influencer Conspiracy:** A theory emerged that game publishers pay 4chan users to generate organic-seeming hype, leveraging the low cost of posting to manipulate public perception.
*   **Indian Diaspora in Japan:** Approximately 2,000 Indian expatriates have offered their homes to athletes competing in the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, responding to local accommodation shortages.

This is a technical diagram comparing the internal structures of a "Leica M240" sensor versus a "Traditional sensor," illustrating how light is processed in each. The diagram is set against a black background. On the left, under the white title "Leica M240," a cross-section shows three adjacent pixel units. Each unit consists of a gray "Pixel" base, a "Photodiode" layer, a colored "Color filter" layer (Green, Red, and Purple from left to right), and a "Microlens" on top. White arrows representing "Incoming light" pass through the microlenses and are directed straight down onto their corresponding photodiodes without obstruction. On the right, under the title "Traditional sensor," a similar cross-section of three pixel units is shown. These also have "Pixel," "Photodiode," "Color filter" (Green, Red, and Purple), and "Microlens" layers. However, white rectangular barriers between the photodiodes cause some of the "Incoming light" (indicated by white and red arrows) to hit the side of the photodiode or be blocked before it reaches the sensor, a phenomenon often referred to as the "shading effect" or "microlens shading." The diagram uses red arrows on the right side specifically to highlight this light loss and redirection.
